title: Himno del atlético de Madrid
why: Written in 1974 by José Aguilar Granados and Ángel Currás García and squarely in copyright. It reached the catalogue labelled CC0-1.0 by whoever uploaded the score, and was admitted because the licence allowlist carried 'granados' as a bare surname for Enrique Granados (d. 1916). The surname now requires the full name; this removes the work that slipped through before it did.

title: Heart and soul remix
why: A remix over Hoagy Carmichael's 1938 tune, who died in 1981, so the composition is under copyright until 2052. Admitted by the same bare 'granados' surname and labelled CC0-1.0 by its uploader, which is exactly what the allowlist exists not to believe.

title: In der weihnachtsbäckerei
why: Written by Rolf Zuckowski in 1987, who is alive, so it is in copyright for a long time yet. The file is worse than that: its own credit line reads 'flowkey version', making it a transcription of a commercial app's arrangement of a copyrighted song. It reached the catalogue labelled CC0-1.0 and was admitted because 'weihnacht' appeared in its title.

title: Weihnachtsmann und co kg theme
why: A television theme, credited to the corpus placeholder 'Misc Soundtrack' and carrying no author at all. Music written for a screen is modern by definition, and the placeholder that should have said so read as anonymity instead. Admitted on 'weihnacht' in its title.

title: The real folk blues
why: The Cowboy Bebop closing theme, written by Yoko Kanno for the Seatbelts in 1998; the file names 'Cowboy Bebop OST' and an arranger. Admitted because its title contains 'folk'.

title: Oh Noel
why: A song by the band I Don't Know How But They Found Me, whose name the file carries along with the transcriber's. Both writers are alive. Admitted because its title contains 'noel'.

title: Animal Crossing City Folk: The City (Evening)
composer: Manaka Tominaga & Shiho Fujii & Kazumi Totaka
why: Nintendo game music from 2008, credited to the three staff composers who wrote it. Admitted because the game is called City Folk and 'folk' appeared in the title.

title: Celtic Hymn
why: Removed as unconfirmable rather than as known copyright, which is the harder call of the six. The score names no composer at all - the manifest credit is the uploader - so there is nothing to date and nothing to check. It may well be their own work released under CC0, which the catalogue would welcome; the allowlist's standing answer is that anything we cannot confirm is dropped, and a smaller safe catalogue beats a larger risky one. Reverse this entry if the composer confirms it is theirs.

title: Coventry carol
why: Credited to "Misc Christmas", which is one of the corpora's filing buckets rather than anybody who wrote it. A composer field naming a category tells a reader nothing and gives the piece no page to belong to. The music is a genuine 16th-century carol and could have been kept by relabelling the credit "Traditional"; removing it is the deliberate choice, since a relabelling would still leave the piece with nobody who wrote it. The import now refuses any credit beginning "Misc", so this is the last of them.
